preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Attacker must have some CHC tokens to demonstrate fee impact

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setBurnFee() and setSwapFee() with excessively high values (e.g., 99). Then perform a token transfer to/from the swapAddress to trigger the fee mechanism, causing disproportionate token burns and liquidity fees that benefit the owner-controlled addresses (deadWallet and liquidityAddress). The high fees effectively steal value from users during transfers.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CitysHome token contract has a fee mechanism that triggers when transfers involve the swapAddress. The owner can set burnFee and liquidityFee to extremely high values (up to 100). When a user transfers tokens to/from the swapAddress, a percentage is burned and another percentage goes to liquidityAddress (which is fixed). The owner can exploit this by: 1) Setting fees to 99 each, 2) Setting swapAddress to an address they control, 3) Performing transfers that trigger the fee mechanism, effectively stealing most of the transferred tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to gain control. 2. Set extremely high fees (99 each). 3. Set swapAddress to an address we control. 4. Transfer tokens to/from the swapAddress to trigger the fee mechanism. 5. The fees will be sent to deadWallet (burn) and liquidityAddress (which we can't control directly, but the contract has ownerWithdrew function to extract from contract balance).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call setBurnFee(99) and setSwapFee(99). 3. Call setSwapAddress() with a controlled address. 4. Get some CHC tokens via deal(). 5. Transfer tokens to swapAddress to trigger the fee mechanism. 6. As owner, use ownerWithdrew to extract tokens from the contract (which received liquidity fees).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has two fee paths: 1) sender == swapAddress, 2) recipient == swapAddress. The recipient path subtracts fees from amount causing underflow with high fees. The sender path transfers fees separately without subtraction, so it won't underflow. We should use the sender path.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Still impersonate owner to set high fees. 2. Set swapAddress to controlled address. 3. Transfer tokens TO the swapAddress first (normal transfer, no fees). 4. Then transfer FROM swapAddress to trigger the sender == swapAddress path which applies fees without subtraction. 5. The fees will be taken from the recipient (attacker), but we can extract value through other means like ownerWithdrew.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner to set fees to 99 each. 2. Set swapAddress. 3. Transfer tokens to swapAddress (normal transfer). 4. Transfer from swapAddress back to attacker (triggers fees). 5. As owner, extract contract balance via ownerWithdrew.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because it used the `recipient == swapAddress` path which causes an arithmetic underflow when fees are set too high (99 + 99 = 198% > 100%). The contract's logic is flawed but we need to work around it by using the `sender == swapAddress` path instead.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract mints 25,000,000 CHC to itself in the constructor. The ownerWithdrew() function allows the owner to withdraw any amount from the contract's balance. This is direct privilege abuse - the owner can steal all tokens from the contract treasury.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner. 2. Call ownerWithdrew() to withdraw all tokens from the contract to the attacker. 3. Verify the attacker's balance increased.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the contract's token balance. 2. Impersonate owner. 3. Call ownerWithdrew with the full balance (divided by 1e18 since function multiplies by 1e18). 4. Check attacker balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous attempts failed because transferring to/from swapAddress triggers fee calculations that cause underflow with 99% fees. The real privilege abuse is simpler: the owner can directly withdraw all tokens from the contract using ownerWithdrew(). The contract has 25,000,000 tokens minted to itself in the constructor.
